long_biography.plain_text:
Taking charge of Raymond in 2000, Gautam Hari Singhania confronted a group burdened by debt and unrelated industrial ventures. He sold the cement, steel and synthetics divisions, used the proceeds to clear liabilities and refocused the company on textiles and apparel. Acquiring ColorPlus then added an established premium-casualwear brand to the portfolio.

A later restructuring separated Raymond's principal businesses into focused listed companies for lifestyle, real estate and engineering. Singhania remains chairman across the resulting group. The structure assigns distinct strategies and management to fashion, property development and engineering, replacing the old conglomerate model with businesses that can be evaluated on their own performance.
